title: Grace pools & throttle playlet — rollout scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick personal playlet for small-surface rollouts where we intentionally use backpressure/grace pools to absorb client spikes and avoid noisy fallback cascades. This is my lightweight checklist + heuristics I can copy into a ticket or Slack when coordinating with SRE and solutions eng.

High-level idea:
- Create two short-lived "grace pools" (GP-A, GP-B) that sit between normal capacity and emergency fallback.
- Use throttles at the request router to divert a controlled fraction of traffic into a grace pool when observed latency or error rate crosses the first threshold.
- Grace pools have more conservative batching (smaller batch sizes), KV warming enabled, and pre-warmed KV caches for top-ten clients. This reduces variance and gives us more predictable tail latency.
- If GP-A becomes saturated, shift small increments of traffic into GP-B and consider auto-eviction for non-critical clients.

Why this differs from standard canary:
- Not testing new model; primarily a safety mechanism for smoothing supply/demand during partial degradation (e.g., noisy GPU node, mem pressure).
- Holds a target SLA for a subset of traffic rather than gradual feature exposure.

Quick decision matrix (one-liners I can paste):
- Latency spike < 50% above baseline and error-rate < 0.5%: route 5% -> GP-A for 15m.
- Latency spike 50-200% or error-rate 0.5-2%: route 10-20% -> GP-A and enable client-level slow-starts for top-5 heavy clients.
- Error-rate > 2% or GP-A saturation for > 10m: enable GP-B at 2-5% and start 1% incremental re-routing from heaviest clients; notify SRE.
- If both GPs saturate or errors > 5%: escalate, initiate rollback or circuit-breaker for non-essential clients, and start page.

Config checklist (practical):
- [ ] Create GP-A / GP-B in runtime config (names, capacity cap = 15% of baseline throughput each).
- [ ] Throttle mapping rule: router.rule.grace_pool = client_id match (fallback catch-all) && latency_probe.metric > threshold.
- [ ] Per-client slow-start: set ramp = 10% initial allowed QPS for first 2m, increase linearly.
- [ ] KV prime list: top-10 client prefixes -> pre-populate cache before opening GP. Run warmup job: /scripts/prime-kv --clients file.csv --pool GP-A.
- [ ] Observability: create dashboard slice: latency_p95, tail_99, errors_5xx, queue_depth, batch_size_mean per pool.
- [ ] Alerts: p95 > baseline*1.5 for 2 consecutive minutes -> alert at P2. queue_depth> 80% cap for 3m -> P1.

Telemetry knobs and thresholds (my current instincts):
- baseline window = 30m of steady traffic before spike. Use rolling median for baseline.
- threshold_1 (probe): p95 > baseline*1.35 OR 5xx rate > 0.3% -> warm GP-A/route 5%.
- threshold_2 (escalate): p95 > baseline*1.7 OR 5xx rate > 1% -> route 15% and enable client slow-starts.
- saturation heuristic: pool_queue_length / pool_capacity > 0.75 for 6m -> consider GP-B.
- eviction policy: evict least-revenue client cohorts (label: non-essential) first.

Runbook snippets (steps to paste in incident chat):
1) "Opening GP-A at 05:12 UTC: routing 5% traffic via router rule grace-pool-A; KV priming started. Observability: watch slice GP-A (p95, queue_depth)."
2) If GP-A p95 > baseline*2 or queue_depth>90%: "Opening GP-B at X; shift incremental 1% buckets from top-3 clients to GP-B; set client kill-switch for test tenant X if still impacted."
3) If both fail: "Execute fast rollback to previous model tag (rollback script) and toggle route back to baseline. Notify on-call SRE and product leads."

Quick rollback command (local devops helper):
- /ops/deploys/rollback-to-tag.sh --service inference --tag v2026-02-15-hotfix --reason "grace pools saturated"
- warm note: confirm tag exists and run a dry-check: /ops/deploys/check-tag.sh v2026-02-15-hotfix

Small helper script (psuedocode to ask infra for):
- curl -X POST $ROUTER/admin/route -d '{"route":"grace-pool-A","weight":5}' --auth-token 
- curl -X POST $INFRAMGMT/pools/create -d '{"name":"GP-A","capacity":0.15,"batch_policy":"conservative"}'
(ask infra to hide sensitive endpoints and wrap into infra cli)

Observation checklist during first 30m after change (timed):
- T+0m: confirm GP-A created, KV priming job finished for top 10 prefixes. Check: kv_miss_rate < 2% for primed prefixes.
- T+2m: p95 should trend down or at least be stable. If p95 increases, evaluate whether batch_size or batch_timeout needs to be lowered.
- T+10m: queue_depth < 50% of cap. If > 70%: open GP-B per escalate matrix.
- T+30m: decide hold (keep), escalate, or roll back. Document decisions in ticket.

Open questions / TODO (talk with Diego/Samir):
- What revenue label mapping do we have to decide eviction order? I want the list and automated mapping to client cohorts.
- Can we create a temporary traffic mirror for GP-A to validate semantics without impacting production (dry mirror)?
- Is there a cheaper preemptible pool we can spin up for GP-B in certain clouds?

Notes to self (less formal):
- Keep the fraction small to avoid oscillation. Small steady diversions are safer than repeated big flips.
- Avoid using this as a canary for model changes — it invites cognitive load. Use separate canary flows.
- For global clients, consider region-aware grace pools; don't centralize a global backpressure pool unless it's cross-region aware.

Postmortem checklist if we hit rollback:
- Time of first knob change, who changed it, and what exact router rule applied.
- GP A/B sizes, queue_depth timeline, top-5 clients hitting fallback.
- Logs: collect sample request IDs for first/last three minutes pre-change and during saturation.
- Evaluation: did smaller batch_size help? or did warm KV matter most?

Snippet for Slack summary i can paste: "Opening small grace-pool experiment: GP-A 5% at 05:12 UTC to absorb latency spike. Watch p95 and queue_depth; escalation rules set (see playlet). If GP-A saturates, we will open GP-B and begin 1% incremental client re-route.

End of scratchpad. Keep short, copy into ticket when needed. Revisit thresholds after two real episodes. "
